title: Verifying CONCESSION already behaves correctly by omission (never a gate, consequence always proceeds)
goal: Confirm, rather than assume, that CONCESSION's absence from lab.common.inference's condition-detection produces the CORRECT behavior (consequence always proceeds regardless of the concession clause's truth) and not some other silent failure mode.
method: Same rule+fact through lab.common.brain.reason, varying only the context passage: affirms the concession clause, contradicts it, or omits it entirely. If CONCESSION is truly never a gate, all three must produce byte-identical output with no 'unresolved' flag.

results_prose: Three contexts (concession clause affirmed, contradicted, absent) produce identical output: True. All three derive the consequence cleanly with no 'unresolved' flag and no blocking: True. Case 1 (affirmed): "MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent. [rule-1] Therefore, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent..". Case 2 (contradicted): "MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent. [rule-1] Therefore, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent..". Case 3 (no context): "MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent. [rule-1] Therefore, it is unlawful although the data subject has given explicit consent..".
conclusion: CONCESSION's omission from lab.common.inference's condition-detection (_find_condition_match only recognizes CONDITION_NEGATIVE/POSITIVE) was already the CORRECT behavior, not an unfixed gap: a concession clause's own truth value genuinely cannot affect whether the consequence proceeds, by definition (that is what 'holds anyway' means), so never checking it against any context is exactly right -- the three cases above are identical because nothing about the context should ever change the outcome. No code change was needed; this exploration exists to verify that claim empirically rather than assume it, the same way EXP-094 verified CAUSAL's omission was already safe before adding its justification field.
scale_down: Only one hand-built rule/fact pair tested, with 'although' specifically -- not swept across 'though'/'even though'/'even if'/'despite', though all five share the same CONCESSION operator and the same _find_condition_match omission, so the same reasoning applies to each.
models_used: spaCy en_core_web_sm dependency parser via lab.common.connectives.find_connectives (unchanged). No NLI call needed -- no exception check ever fires for a CONCESSION clause, which is exactly the point being verified. No generative model.
